behavior.assessment: The added step runs mypy on typecheck_probe.pyi, redirects output to typecheck-negative.log, requires a non-zero mypy exit, and then requires the exact substring 'TypedDict item ...'.

consumer.assessment: The tests job in the Harness verification GitHub Actions workflow consumes this step; a grep failure fails that CI job, which runs on push, pull_request, and workflow_dispatch.

impact.assessment: Precondition: mypy exits non-zero but its output no longer contains the exact substring. Then grep fails while the redirected diagnostic is not displayed, causing a CI failure that is harder to distinguish from a real contract regression.

semantic_assessment.summary: The diff adds a CI probe that runs mypy with output redirected then greps for an exact diagnostic substring. The head workflow shows this in the tests job, so the CI consumer is established. The evidence supports the stated maintainability impact: if mypy still rejects the probe but changes wording, the grep can fail without the diagnostic being displayed, subject to that precondition.

specific_strengths.detail: This improves static alignment and readability for the report renderer without introducing a new runtime import dependency or removing payload validation.

finding_candidates.rule_or_contract: Maintainability: avoid duplicated sources of truth for stable internal contracts.

future_guidance.detail: Consider narrowing stage protocol state to RunState where practical so static checks can catch more state-shape mismatches across stage boundaries.

future_guidance.title: Narrow Any-typed stage state where practical

future_guidance.title: Add a separate negative fixture for Required task_id

future_guidance.detail: When stable stage callables exist for StageBoundary and TaskStageBoundary, consider adding corresponding bindings to the positive fixture for broader signature coverage.

future_guidance.title: Extend positive protocol bindings when stable callables exist

future_guidance.detail: As high-churn record shapes stabilize, consider replacing selected dict[str, object] and Any fields with narrower TypedDict or union types to improve readability.

future_guidance.title: Narrow high-churn contract fields as schemas stabilize

specific_strengths.detail: The change makes the state container's intended data shapes more reviewable and gives stage authors clearer contracts without adding runtime validation behavior.
specific_strengths.observation: RunState fields now reference SnapshotRecord, PlanRecord, TaskRecord, ReviewResult, LedgerEntry, and related TypedDict names instead of bare dict in the changed lines.
specific_strengths.title: Named typed records replace bare dict annotations at key state boundaries

specific_strengths.detail: Explicit boundary signatures can reduce coupling between the controller and stage implementations and make signature drift easier to detect in type-checked fixtures.
specific_strengths.observation: The change introduces PlannerBoundary, StageBoundary, TaskStageBoundary, AttemptStartBoundary, AttemptFinishBoundary, ReconcileBoundary, and ReportBoundary protocols.
specific_strengths.title: Protocol declarations make stage boundaries explicit

specific_strengths.detail: A self-documenting negative fixture makes the intended type-check failure clear to future maintainers and reduces accidental repair of a deliberate failure case.
specific_strengths.observation: typecheck_probe.pyi states in its docstring that it is a negative mypy fixture and encodes an invalid TaskRecord assignment with a string unit_ids value.
specific_strengths.title: Negative type fixture is self-documenting

specific_strengths.detail: Binding real implementation callables to the declared protocols creates a concrete static check that boundary signatures remain compatible as code evolves.
specific_strengths.observation: typed_boundary_probe.pyi assigns plan_review, consolidate_findings, render_report, start_attempt_stage, and finish_attempt_stage to their corresponding Protocol types.
specific_strengths.title: Positive boundary probe binds real callables to protocols

specific_strengths.detail: Stating the boundary prevents readers from mistaking static annotations for runtime validation and supports fail-closed behavior at external edges.
specific_strengths.observation: typed_contracts.pyi explicitly says the declarations are type-only and do not validate JSON, provider, or workflow input, and that external validators remain authoritative.
specific_strengths.title: Type-only contracts state their validation limits

finding_candidates.consequence: As more typed-contract checks are added, fixture changes must be replicated manually and can silently diverge across tests.
finding_candidates.observation: The new contract-key test embeds a repeated sequence of inline git subprocess commands and rev-parse calls directly in the test body. Future contract tests needing a real collected snapshot must copy or diverge from this setup instead of sharing one focused fixture, increasing maintenance drift risk.
finding_candidates.rule_or_contract: Prefer cohesive test fixture helpers when setup is reused or likely to grow.
finding_candidates.title: Inline git fixture setup in contract-key test

specific_strengths.detail: It makes typed-contract drift visible at test boundaries rather than relying only on hand-built fixtures.
specific_strengths.observation: The change updates RunState annotation expectations to SnapshotRecord/PlanRecord and adds an end-to-end key-coverage check against real collected snapshot and plan outputs.
specific_strengths.title: Contract drift made visible

specific_strengths.detail: This makes boundary-contract drift fail closed in CI rather than silently passing.
specific_strengths.observation: The workflow adds a negative mypy probe that explicitly fails if the wrong-shape boundary record unexpectedly passes and then verifies the expected diagnostic text.
specific_strengths.title: Fail-closed type boundary probe
